parts.watchFor: Yusuf has a dream. Watch what his father tells him to do with it.

questions.q: Which of his sons did Yaqub love most?
options: Yusuf and Binyamin, the two youngest

questions.q: What did Yusuf see in his dream?
options: Eleven stars, the sun and the moon

questions.q: What did his father tell him to do?
options: Keep the dream from his brothers

lesson.text: Yaqub saw the envy among his sons and told Yusuf to keep his dream private. Not every blessing needs to be shared with everyone: wisdom protects hearts, your own and others'.
lesson.curious: Muslims learn from Yaqub (Jacob) that some good news is best kept private where it might stir envy.

reflect.muslim: Is there something you share online that might stir envy, or that you'd be wiser to keep private?
reflect.curious: Why might it be wise to keep some good news to yourself?

parts.act: Keep one good thing private this week, and thank God for it quietly.

parts.watchFor: Yusuf's brothers throw him into a well. Watch who is with him in the dark.

questions.q: Why did the brothers throw Yusuf into the well?
What was Yusuf inspired with, alone in the well?
options: That one day he would tell them what they had done
That he should forget his family

questions.q: What happened to Yusuf in Egypt?
options: He was sold cheaply, for a few coins

lesson.text: Alone in the dark of the well, Yusuf was not alone: God told him this was not the end. Your lowest moment can be the start of something God is building.
lesson.curious: In the Quran's telling, Yusuf (Joseph) was comforted in the well by God's promise that his story was not over. Muslims take hope from it in their own dark moments.

reflect.muslim: What's the darkest moment you've been through? Can you see now anything God was building in it?
reflect.curious: Has a low point in your life ever led somewhere good?

parts.act: When something goes wrong this week, say: beautiful patience, and God is the one whose help is sought.

parts.watchFor: In Egypt, Yusuf is tempted and wronged. Watch what he chooses each time.

questions.q: What did Yusuf say when the doors were closed on him?
options: I will do as you say

questions.q: How did the torn shirt show Yusuf was telling the truth?
options: It was torn at the front
It was torn at the back

questions.q: What did Yusuf do before explaining the prisoners' dreams?

lesson.text: Yusuf chose prison over doing wrong, and even in prison he spoke to others about God. Self-control and faith go with you into any room.
lesson.curious: Yusuf's story in the Quran shows him choosing prison over wrongdoing, and still caring for others while unjustly locked up.

reflect.muslim: Where are you most tempted? What's your way of saying "I seek refuge in God" there?
reflect.curious: What helps you say no when everyone around you is saying yes?

parts.act: When you're tempted this week, say a'udhu billah (I seek refuge in God) and walk away.

parts.watchFor: The king has a dream nobody can explain. Watch what Yusuf asks for before he leaves prison.

questions.q: What did the king dream of?
options: Seven fat cows eaten by seven lean ones

questions.q: Why did Yusuf at first refuse to leave prison?
options: He wanted his name cleared first
He was afraid of the king

questions.q: What did Yusuf ask to be put in charge of?

lesson.text: Yusuf made sure his name was cleared, then used his knowledge to save a whole land from famine. Plan in good times for hard ones, and use your skills to serve others.
lesson.curious: Yusuf's plan of storing grain in good years for the famine is remembered in Islam, as in the Bible, as wisdom put to the service of others.

reflect.muslim: Which skill has God given you that you could use to serve others?
reflect.curious: What are you good at that could help other people?

parts.act: Use a skill you have to help someone this week, without being asked.

parts.watchFor: The brothers stand before Yusuf, not knowing who he is. Watch what he does with his power.

questions.q: What did Yaqub never give up, even in his grief?
What did Yusuf say to his brothers?
What did Yaqub ask his sons before he died?
options: What will you worship after me?

lesson.text: Yaqub never lost hope in God's mercy. Yusuf forgave the brothers who had thrown him in a well, and the dream came true. Never despair of God's mercy, and forgive when you have the power not to.
lesson.curious: The story ends with forgiveness: Yusuf pardons his brothers and the family is reunited. Muslims learn never to despair of God's mercy.

carry.title: Yusuf's prayer at the end of his story

reflect.muslim: Who do you need to forgive? Who do you need to ask forgiveness from?
reflect.curious: Is there someone you could forgive, even partly? What would it free in you?

parts.act: Forgive one person this week, out loud or in your heart, and pray for them.
